title: Affine nonvanishing loci imply ampleness
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, put $X_s=\{x\in X:s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})_x\}$, where $\mathfrak m_x$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-residue-field]. If for every $x\in X$ there are $n\geq1$ and $s$ such that $x$ belongs to the affine open $X_s$, then $\mathcal L$ is ample in the sense of [def-sc-ample]: some positive tensor power of $\mathcal L$ has a complete linear system giving a closed immersion into projective space over $k$.

source.place: Properties, Definition 01PS (definition-ample): the affine nonvanishing-locus criterion; Morphisms, Lemma 01VT (lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample), (1) implies (5), with base Spec(k), using Lemma 01VK (lemma-ample-over-affine). Since X is proper and projective space is separated, the resulting immersion is closed. The complete-linear-system morphism is also a closed immersion: extend its finite defining sections to a basis of H^0(X,L^d), project back to the original linear system on the open where those coordinates do not simultaneously vanish, and use properness to make this immersion closed.
